operations.specification:
This operation creates a new user account in the Todo List application by inserting a distinct record into the `todo_list_users` table, which acts as the single identity and actor entity for all business logic. The operation expects a unique email address and a securely hashed password; on successful registration, a JWT access token is issued for immediate authenticated use. All registered users have strict privacy and sole data ownership, with no guest role supported. Registration is the only entry into the authenticated system and is public, requiring both email and password fields. Extra fields such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are automatically managed by the database. The API specifically references the `email` and `password_hash` columns of `todo_list_users`. Each join event is logged for audit and security compliance.

The endpoint is public and does not require prior authentication. Appropriate validation ensures email uniqueness, proper password hashing, and audit logging for account creation events. Soft deletion capability is managed by the `deleted_at` field but is unrelated to this operation.

Successful creation returns an authentication payload, including issued JWT tokens and relevant registration metadata, conforming strictly to the schema. Security events, such as failed or duplicate registrations, are handled with clear error responses. This endpoint is the absolute prerequisite for all login and token refresh flows.

The operation does not interact with other business tables or sessions; session creation occurs only upon post-registration authentication.

This operation should be used in conjunction with the login endpoint for future access and with the token refresh endpoint for session continuity.
operations.description:
This API operation enables new user registration by creating a record in the `todo_list_users` table, which represents each registered end-user in the Todo List application. The request must provide a unique email and a securely hashed password, ensuring that only verified credentials allow access to the service.

Security considerations include enforcing uniqueness of `email`, hashing of passwords using current best cryptographic standards, and immediate audit of registration attempts. The table's `created_at` and `updated_at` fields record the registration and any future account changes, while the `deleted_at` field provides a soft-deletion mechanism, which is not triggered by this endpoint.

This endpoint ties directly to the single actor identity of the Todo List application, ensuring each account is separate and cannot view or modify other users' data. All business task ownership, session records, and interactions track back to this primary key.

Validation rules enforce proper email format, case-insensitive uniqueness, and reject registrations that attempt to reuse deleted or existing addresses. Account creation is always a public operation and requires no existing authentication.

The endpoint is critical to the authentication workflow: registration must precede all login or session management, making this the foundational endpoint for onboarding new users.
operations.summary: Register a new user in the todo_list_users table.

requestBody.description: New user registration fields, including unique email and password (plain, to be hashed server-side).

responseBody.description: Authentication payload including JWT token and user metadata.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
This operation authenticates a registered user account using the credentials stored in the `todo_list_users` table. By providing a valid email and password combination, users can obtain new JWT access and refresh tokens representing their active session. This endpoint is required for all users to transition from unauthenticated to authenticated states and underpins the entirety of the account security model for the Todo List system.

The authentication process involves securely comparing the supplied password to the `password_hash` stored in the database, utilizing established, secure password hashing algorithms. Email is enforced as a unique identifier, and the endpoint performs constant-time lookup and validation. Successful authentication leads to issuance of a new session record in the `todo_list_user_sessions` table, capturing forensic data such as login timestamp, IP address, and connection details for audit and investigation. The operation also automatically manages session lifecycle and concurrency based on associated session table policies.

Authentication failures—due to invalid email, password mismatch, or account soft deletion via `deleted_at`—result in clear error responses. Audit logs and session data capture all access attempts for monitoring, rate limiting, and security incident tracing. The endpoint does not expose any user information directly except through the authenticated token payload.

The operation only issues tokens for fully validated credentials and never reveals whether an account exists; errors are generic for privacy. Only users registered via `/auth/user/join` are eligible. The session and user tables cooperate, with session creation depending on valid user authentication.
operations.description:
Authenticate a user using credentials in the `todo_list_users` table, validating their unique email and password. Passwords are never stored or transmitted in plain text but always processed as secure hashes. This operation interacts with the `password_hash` and `email` columns for verification and relies on `deleted_at` to determine if accounts are eligible for login.

Security considerations include constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks, full audit logging through session insertion in the `todo_list_user_sessions` schema, and avoidance of explicit existence confirmation for any user account.

The endpoint ties every session and all business data ownership in the application back to a valid, authenticated user record. Audit requirements drive full contextual session logging.

Input validation rejects malformed or non-unique emails and fails authentication if the supplied credentials do not match. The endpoint is fully public and does not require prior authentication.

This operation must be used in conjunction with registration for account onboarding and with token refresh for session continuity.
operations.summary: Authenticate user and issue JWT token (todo_list_users table).

requestBody.description: Login credentials for authentication, including registered email and password (plain, for server-side verification).

responseBody.description: Authentication payload with JWT token and user metadata, issued upon successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
This operation refreshes a previously issued JWT token using a valid refresh token accompanying an active user session, as recorded in the `todo_list_user_sessions` schema. It is essential for maintaining uninterrupted authenticated client activity without requiring repeated password entry. The operation only proceeds if the submitted refresh token corresponds to an active, unexpired session linked to a valid user in the `todo_list_users` table (with `deleted_at` null).

On success, the endpoint issues a new access token and optionally rotates the refresh token, while updating relevant session metadata (timestamps) in `todo_list_user_sessions`. Expired, invalid, or revoked refresh tokens trigger appropriate error responses and may prompt client-side reauthentication workflows. The endpoint never reveals specific failure causes for privacy.

The endpoint performs all validation server-side using true session data; the client must not supply user credentials but only the refresh token. On the database, session and user records are cross-checked for validity and active status.
operations.description:
Refresh an existing user session's JWT access token using a valid refresh token, with all user and session validation handled against `todo_list_user_sessions` and `todo_list_users` tables. Successful refresh issues a new access token and updates session timestamps and audit metadata.

Privacy is maintained by never disclosing whether a session or user still exists; errors give no additional information. The endpoint supports continuous access security by limiting session lifetimes and granting users flexible authentication continuity with strong integrity.

This operation is core to supporting modern SPA and mobile session lifecycles.

Input is strictly limited to a valid refresh token, and output is a new authentication payload in standard format. No user credentials are required for this flow, and the endpoint is available only to clients already holding a valid refresh token associated with an active session.
operations.summary: Refresh user JWT token using session (todo_list_user_sessions table).

requestBody.description: Refresh token for current session, linked securely to user/session records.

responseBody.description: Authentication payload with new access token and associated metadata.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the detailed information of the currently authenticated user by referencing the todo_list_users table. It allows a logged-in user to access their own full user profile, including identification, email address, and account metadata. The retrieval operation ensures privacy by returning only the details for the account associated with the active authentication token; no user may access information about any other account. This endpoint is fundamental for supporting self-service actions and validating the user's current profile context within the Todo List service.
operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated user's own account information from the Todo List service.

This operation is designed for end-users to inspect their own identity, profile, and account audit details, using the login context from their session. Only the current user's data will ever be returned, and authorization is strictly enforced.

Fields include unique user ID, email address, timestamps of creation and most recent update, as well as deleted_at if the account is in a soft-deleted state. No sensitive fields such as raw password are available from this endpoint. This operation forms the basis for all user-driven account management features within the service.
operations.summary: Retrieve authenticated user's own account details (todo_list_users).

responseBody.description: The authenticated user's full account information from todo_list_users.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation allows the currently authenticated user to update their own account details in the todo_list_users table. Users may modify updatable fields such as their email address (subject to uniqueness and verification), as well as change their password. The operation strictly restricts which fields can be updated, following the todo_list_users schema and enforcing uniqueness and validation requirements. Only the user themselves may perform this update, never on behalf of another user.
operations.description:
Update specific details of the currently authenticated user's account in the Todo List service.

Permissible updates include changing the email address (with required uniqueness and format constraints) and updating the password, which is securely re-hashed and never exposed in plaintext. The operation enforces attribute-level validation according to the todo_list_users schema, and logs all changes for audit and security purposes.

Strict security is ensured: the update may be performed only by the authenticated user, with no cross-user updates possible from this endpoint. Account updates are atomic and return the revised account information upon success.

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the current authenticated user's account. Only mutable fields from todo_list_users are included.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes the authenticated user's own account from the todo list system. It removes the user record from the primary user table (`todo_list_users`) and irreversibly deletes all tasks and session data linked to this user. The operation validates that the request is properly authenticated and verifies ownership before proceeding. Account deletion triggers cascading removal of all todos (from `todo_list_todos`) and user sessions (from `todo_list_user_sessions`), fully honoring the application’s privacy, business rules, and data minimization commitments.
operations.description:
Permanently delete the currently authenticated user's account along with all personal data including todos and session history.

This operation can only be performed by a user on their own account. Cross-account deletion is strictly forbidden. Upon invocation, the system verifies that the caller is authenticated and that the user matches the session. If authentication fails or the user is not found, an error response is issued without revealing user existence information.

When deletion is successful, all todos owned by the user (from the `todo_list_todos` table) are deleted. Active and historical session records (from the `todo_list_user_sessions`) are removed to ensure complete data minimization and compliance with privacy requirements. There is no recovery or soft-deletion—this is a hard, permanent remove. Rate limiting and audit logging are applied to prevent abuse or accidental mass deletions.

This action supersedes any pending operations for the user; all pending tasks and sessions are cleared. The operation ends the authenticated session and invalidates all access tokens, immediately logging the user out after completion. No further actions can be performed once the account is deleted.
operations.summary: Delete the authenticated user's `todo_list_users` account and all associated data.
operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated list of authentication sessions belonging to the currently logged-in user by querying the `todo_list_user_sessions` table. Sessions provide information about active, expired, and historical logins, including metadata such as IP, connection URL, timestamps, and device information. The operation supports advanced filtering for session status, creation or expiry date, and login origin to enable users to audit their own account access and monitor for suspicious activity. Only sessions belonging to the authenticated user are included; all others are strictly excluded for security and privacy compliance.
operations.description:
Return a filtered, paginated list of all authentication sessions for the current user, including both active and historical sessions.

The requesting user must be authenticated. The operation validates ownership and restricts results to sessions owned by the current user (foreign key `todo_list_user_sessions.todo_list_user_id`). Query options allow filtering by session start or expiration date, associated IP address, or connection URL. The query results include all required fields for audit and review, consistent with the schema constraints (IP, referrer, URL, timestamps).

This API empowers users to review their session history for possible unauthorized access, expired sessions, or security issues. Only the authenticated user's own sessions are accessible—no cross-user exposure is permitted. Rate limiting and request validation are enforced for safe, performant querying. This endpoint is fully aligned with privacy, audit, and data minimization policies described in the requirements documentation.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated, filtered list of user's own session records in `todo_list_user_sessions`.

requestBody.description: Filter or search criteria for the authenticated user's session query, supporting multiple fields including creation/expiration range, IP, and origin.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of session records belonging to the authenticated user.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information about a specific login session for the currently authenticated Todo List end-user. It operates on the todo_list_user_sessions table, which logs every authenticated session with forensic data such as IP, creation/expiry, and referrer. The sessionId parameter identifies the precise session record. This endpoint supports user review/audit of their own active and past sessions, enhancing transparency and empowering personal account security monitoring. Session visibility is strictly limited: users may access only their own sessions, validated both via path context and backend business logic using parent user linkage. This read-only resource is essential for audit history, security-conscious users, and supporting concurrent login tracing.
operations.description:
Retrieve full forensic details about a single login session belonging to the currently authenticated user in the Todo List application.

This operation is crucial for security transparency, allowing users to confirm their own session activity, monitor concurrent logins, and investigate unusual account access. The response reveals connection metadata (IP, referrer, creation/expiry) as stored in the todo_list_user_sessions table, with all business rules regarding confidentiality and privacy enforced—users are strictly barred from querying sessions not owned by them.

Permission is strictly scoped to authenticated owners: the path and session record must match the identity of the requester as determined by authentication tokens and data isolation logic. If the session does not exist or is not owned by the current user, a not found or forbidden error is returned. Logging and audit support is maintained for all access attempts. Integration: This operation is commonly paired with GET /users/self and PATCH /users/self/sessions for session management dashboards and security review workflows.
operations.summary: Retrieve details of a specific user session from todo_list_user_sessions.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the user session record, scoped to the currently authenticated user.

responseBody.description: Full details of the user session including IP, referrer, creation/expiry, and ownership linkage.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation immediately terminates (logs out) a specific login session for the currently authenticated Todo List user, removing it from the active session set in the todo_list_user_sessions table. It is intentionally limited to self-owned sessions, enforcing strict data isolation and prohibiting users from terminating sessions of others. Session termination updates the session record's expired_at timestamp to reflect the logout event and ensures that subsequent requests using that session become invalid. This provides users with explicit control over session security, allowing for immediate revocation if a device or location is no longer trusted. The operation directly supports proactive account security and aligns with best practice personal session management, following the audit and logging requirements identified in schema comments.
operations.description:
Terminate an active or historical login session for the authenticated Todo List user by sessionId. Executing this operation sets the expired_at field in the todo_list_user_sessions database table for the identified session, representing a user-initiated logout and invalidating the session token for future requests.

Users may invoke this endpoint to close any of their current or historic sessions, providing critical account protection in cases of lost devices, suspicious logins, or to enforce exclusive access. The server verifies the user owns the session before updating and logs the action for audit and security compliance. No action is taken if the session does not exist or is unauthorized, and feedback is provided according to security best practices. Deletion does not remove the record entirely but marks session termination for ongoing forensic traceability.

This operation is fundamental to session security, offering users instantaneous revocation of session credentials. It is designed to work in concert with session GET and PATCH endpoints for complete user-driven session lifecycle management.
operations.summary: Terminate a specific user session (logout) in todo_list_user_sessions.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the session to terminate, restricted to the authenticated user's own sessions.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated and filterable list of todo tasks from the todo_list_todos table, which represents the main business tasks of the Todo List Application. The API provides robust search capabilities, supporting filters such as task status (completed or pending), creation date, due date, and text search on the todo title or description. Pagination parameters allow clients to request specific pages and control batch size, supporting efficient display in client UIs. This API is designed to handle large sets of tasks and returns summary views optimized for list rendering, not full task detail. It references the ITodoListTodo.IRequest request type for search criteria and the IPageITodoListTodo.ISummary response type for paginated results. CRUD operations for creation, updating, and deletion are provided in separate endpoints.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated, filterable list of todos from todo_list_todos
operations.description:
Request a list of todo tasks, filtered and paginated according to advanced user-defined criteria. The client may filter todos by completion status, time window, or perform a search on title/description fields. Pagination controls (page, pageSize) enable scalable handling of large datasets, and sort options allow prioritizing specific tasks for display.

All returned data is sourced from the todo_list_todos table, which holds all user-generated todos. The schema provides fields for basic metadata, due/completed flags, and optional notes. This operation is optimal for rendering todo overviews or preview cards in applications.

To ensure secure and private data handling, the operation will filter results to only include tasks owned by or shared with the authenticated user (enforced at the business logic/service layer, not in input). Administrative users may search all records; normal users will see only their own. Related endpoints include single-todo fetch, create, update, and erase for detailed management workflows.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination parameters for listing todos, using the ITodoListTodo.IRequest DTO.

responseBody.description: Paginated, filtered list of todo summary records matching the search criteria, as IPageITodoListTodo.ISummary.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the full details of a specific todo item, referenced by its unique identifier, from the todo_list_todos table. The API returns all available fields for the requested todo, including metadata, completion status, due date, and user notes. The todoId path parameter identifies the target todo and must be a valid UUID corresponding to an existing record. This API is read-only and provides comprehensive information suitable for editing forms or detail displays. The response is fully aligned with the ITodoListTodo contract, modeling the business entity as defined in the Prisma schema.
operations.summary: Fetch full detail for a single todo by ID from todo_list_todos
operations.description:
Retrieve all available data for a specific todo task using its unique identifier as a path parameter. This endpoint is used for opening detail views, supporting edit forms, or displaying task information in full context to the user. The response contains all fields stored in the todo_list_todos schema.

Security is enforced so that only the owner or authorized collaborators may access non-administrative tasks; attempts to fetch others' tasks will result in access denial unless the authenticated actor holds administrative privileges.

This operation is designed for single-resource reads. For list displays and search, use the paginated todos endpoint. For modifying or deleting a todo, use the update or erase endpoints, respectively.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo, as a UUID string.

responseBody.description: Complete todo item details as returned from ITodoListTodo.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A todo task must be created first using this operation before it can be fetched by its ID.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo task for the authenticated user in the system. The operation operates on the todo_list_todos table and supports business rules such as required titles between 1 and 100 characters, optional descriptions, a default completion status of false, and an optional due date. User identity is determined via authentication; the todo is assigned to this user via foreign key. Field-level validation is strictly enforced before creating the record. The created todo is immediately persisted with timestamps for audit purposes. Duplicate detection on title + due date is enforced for each user by the unique index.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item belonging to the authenticated user. This endpoint enables users to add actionable business tasks to their personal todo list. Each todo must include a brief title that is between 1 and 100 characters; descriptions are optional, supporting up to 600 characters if provided. The completion status defaults to false and can be updated later; a due date is optional and, if supplied, must be a current or future ISO 8601 date.

Only authenticated users may create new todos; ownership is enforced, and users cannot assign todos to other users. Any attempt to submit an invalid payload—such as missing a required title, using a duplicate title for the same due date, or setting a due date in the past—will be rejected with a clear error message. Submission also records creation and update times automatically for history and sorting purposes.

This operation directly persists todo data in the todo_list_todos table with a unique index on [user, title, due_date] to prevent accidental duplicate task entries. Related endpoints: update an existing todo (PUT /todos/{todoId}), delete a todo (DELETE /todos/{todoId}), and search todos (PATCH /todos).
operations.summary: Create a new todo task (todo_list_todos table) owned by the authenticated user.

requestBody.description: Data for creating a new todo task: title (required), description (optional), completed (defaults to false), due_date (optional).

responseBody.description: Detailed information of the created todo task, including all fields after persistence.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates a single todo belonging to the authenticated user, specifically targeting the todo_list_todos table. The todo is located via its unique UUID primary key (todoId). The endpoint supports modifying the title, description, completion status, and due date, applying all relevant business rules and data constraints as enforced in the schema. All requested changes are validated; for example, titles must remain 1–100 characters, and descriptions cannot exceed 600 characters. Record timestamps are updated upon modification, supporting audit trails and user-facing task timelines. Ownership is strictly enforced such that users may only update their own todos, never those belonging to others.
operations.description:
Update an existing todo item owned by the authenticated user. This endpoint allows modification of key todo task attributes such as the title, the optional long description, the completion status (true or false), and the optional due date. Business rules such as title length, description maximum length, and due date validation are strictly enforced at both the application and persistence layer.

To update a todo, the user must specify the todo's unique UUID identifier in the path. If the specified todo does not exist or does not belong to the user, the operation is rejected with a not-found or forbidden response. On successful update, the todo's updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed. Ownership validation ensures data privacy and prevents unauthorized modification of other users' tasks.

This operation persists all changes to the todo_list_todos table and is intended for granular task management. Related endpoints include task creation (POST /todos) and todo deletion (DELETE /todos/{todoId}).
operations.summary: Update an existing todo task by its UUID (todo_list_todos table).

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target todo item the user wishes to update.

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the specified todo task: title (required), description (optional), completed, and due_date as applicable.

responseBody.description: Detailed information of the updated todo, reflecting all recent changes.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A todo must be created before it can be updated. The POST operation initializes a todo in the system and assigns it a unique todoId, which the update endpoint requires as a path parameter.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes a business todo task from the todo_list_todos table in the core Todo List Application. The operation targets exactly one todo, identified by its unique identifier (UUID) in the path parameter. It enforces strict data ownership: only the owner of the todo (resolved via the todo's todo_list_user_id field) may delete their own todo; cross-user deletion is prohibited by business logic and foreign key constraints.

Permanent deletion is applied, meaning the record is removed from the database with no soft-deletion or restoration workflow, as explicitly stated by business requirements and the Prisma schema comments. Only authorized, authenticated users may use this endpoint. Attempts to delete non-existent records or records owned by other users result in appropriate error responses and are never permitted through misuse of this API.

Related endpoints include PATCH /todos for listing/searching todos, and POST /todos for creating new tasks. This DELETE operation cleanly removes tasks that are no longer needed from the user's personal todo store, in compliance with audit and data lifecycle policies.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a todo from todo_list_todos by its unique identifier.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a single todo task from the system for its owner user. This action irreversibly deletes a business todo from persistent storage.

This endpoint enforces owner-only access—only the authenticated user who owns the todo (as referenced by todo_list_user_id) is allowed to perform the deletion. If a user attempts to delete a todo owned by another user, the request is denied with an authorization error. If the target todo does not exist, a not found error is returned to maintain business integrity.

This operation interacts directly with the todo_list_todos database table, using the todo's universally unique identifier (UUID) as path parameter. As the application follows strict data isolation, deleted todos are fully removed (no soft deletion) with no opportunity for recovery after completion. Security and audit compliance are maintained by logging deletion events. This operation is typically used in conjunction with list, detail, and create endpoints as part of a complete user todo management workflow.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target todo record to be permanently deleted.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

ITodoListUser.IJoin.description:
Request DTO for new user registration (join) in the Todo List Application.

Defines the required information to register a unique, authenticated end-user. Only the email and password fields are required, reflecting strict business and security constraints from requirements and Prisma schema. Password is provided in plain text for secure server-side hashing before storage; never accept `password_hash` directly from the client. Additional metadata and session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are included for audit and security per MVP operation and session logging policies. Id, timestamps, and deletion markers are managed by the system and must not appear in client request bodies.

This type is directly mapped to the `todo_list_users` Prisma schema (user registration table); it is the mandatory prerequisite for all login and session lifecycle operations. All business, validation, security, and privacy constraints are enforced via this type.

email.description: Email address used for user login and as the unique global identifier. Must be valid per RFC 5322, enforced as case-insensitive unique index in the database. Required for registration, authentication, and account recovery. Cannot be changed after account creation.

password.description: Plain-text password for registration. Must be 8-255 characters, contain at least one letter and one number. Hashing and salt are performed server-side before storing in the password_hash field in the database. This field is never stored or returned as-is.

oneOf.description: Client IP address used for the registration session (if available). Used for audit and session security. Optional, must be valid IPv4 or IPv6; empty or null means server will infer from request context.

Client IP address used for the registration session (if available). Used for audit and session security. Optional, must be valid IPv4 or IPv6; empty or null means server will infer from request context.

ip.description: Optional client IP address at registration, for session and security audit. Often inferred from HTTP request if omitted.

href.description: URL of the registration page/session as seen by the client. Used for session context logging, audit, and security correlation. Must be provided by the client at join time. Required for session creation and forensic investigation.

referrer.description: Referrer URL leading to registration. Used for session context, audit trail, and analysis. Required to fully trace session provenance. Must be provided by the client at join time.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication payload object for successful user registration, login, or token refresh.

Returns the actor's unique identifier, JWT access and refresh tokens, and contextual metadata for authenticated session management. Used as the response type for join, login, and refresh endpoints. Directly linked to the todo_list_users (user) table for id field, and to session creation context for issued tokens.

Includes only safe, public fields; sensitive data such as password hashes is never present. All properties conform to best security practices and directly support every client-side session and authentication use case for the Todo List application.

id.description: Unique user identifier corresponding to the primary key in the todo_list_users table. Used as the actor reference for all request/response flows and access control.

email.description: Email associated with this authenticated user. Used as the principal identifier for client display and session context.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when the user account was first created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last modification to user account data (e.g., password or email update). Always present.

oneOf.description: Soft deletion marker—if set, account is being deleted and access is denied.
If not deleted, field is null.

deleted_at.description: Null unless account is soft-deleted. Present for audit and recovery.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
User authentication (login) request for the Todo List app.

Used to authenticate an end-user against their unique email and password, as recorded in the todo_list_users table. The request captures the plain-text password for secure server-side hashing and comparison, and tracks session context for auditing and session creation. The login endpoint issues new JWT tokens to access todo APIs upon successful credentials verification.

All fields are required. The client must provide the email, password, and connection context. User identities are managed only through this mechanism; actor and system IDs come from authenticated JWT after login. This operation must be performed before accessing any protected resources.

email.description: User's unique email address for authentication and account recovery. Enforced unique and case-insensitive in the database. Must be a valid RFC 5322 email address.

password.description: Plain-text user password for login verification. Used only during authentication and not stored or transmitted beyond server-side hash comparison. Must match the value used during registration.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for session tracking and audit. Optional; can be extracted by server if not provided.
IP may be null if unavailable, but best practice to provide for audit.

ip.description: Client IP address optional; server may infer if omitted. Used for new session record (todo_list_user_sessions) upon successful login.

href.description: Full connection URL (the page or route where the login occurred). Provides important investigation and audit context for the session. Required, must be a valid URI.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page or source, if any) captured at login. Enables audit of session initiation funnel and context. Required and must be a valid URI, even if empty string.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Refresh JWT authentication session for Todo List app users.

Used by authenticated clients to exchange a valid refresh token for a new access token. Ties closely to the todo_list_user_sessions table and ensures the user is still valid and active. Secures ongoing access without requiring the user's email or password again. Maintains seamless, secure user experience for long-lived sessions.

Supplied refresh token must correspond to an active session; errors are generic for privacy. Input is strictly limited to the single required token field.

refresh_token.description: Refresh token (opaque string) representing an active, unexpired user session. Must correspond to a valid record in todo_list_user_sessions, and is single-use if token rotation policy applies.

ITodoListUser.description:
Authenticated Todo List service user account entity.

Represents a single registered user within the Todo List application. This type is returned when retrieving the authenticated user's account details. Includes unique ID, email, (soft) deletion status, and audit timestamps. Passwords, hashes, and any sensitive authentication context are excluded for security. Each user owns their own todos; direct relations are not included in this DTO, keeping strict privacy boundaries between users.

Field and business rules are derived directly from the todo_list_users Prisma model. Data isolation and actor boundaries are strictly enforced—no cross-account access is ever possible via API or DTO structure.

id.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each user account. Read-only.

email.description: Unique email address for login. Case-insensitive. Required, enforced unique in app and DB. Never exposed to other users.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when the user account was first created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last modification to user account data (e.g., password or email update). Always present.

oneOf.description: Soft deletion marker—if set, account is being deleted and access is denied.
If not deleted, field is null.

deleted_at.description: Null unless account is soft-deleted. Present for audit and recovery.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
Payload for updating the authenticated user's Todo List account.

Allows a logged-in user to modify mutable fields of their own profile. Only fields allowed by business rules—email and password—are included. Fields are validated per application and database schema; email must be unique and valid, password is plain for secure rehash and storage. System-manages ID and timestamps are excluded. Only the user themselves may perform this update, and actor identity is taken from authentication context, not request data.

All fields are optional and individually updatable. Business rules: At least one field must be provided. Email and password updates are atomic and return the new account info upon success.

email.description: New email address for account (optional). Must be valid and unique; case-insensitive. Only updatable by account owner.

password.description: New password for account (optional). Plain. Backend will securely hash before storage. Must pass security policy (min-length, complexity). Only updatable by owner.

ITodoListUserSession.description: A record of an authenticated user session in the Todo List service, supporting security review, personal audit, and privacy transparency.

id.description: Primary key. Uniquely identifies each authentication session. This value is required for session tracing and forensic review.

todo_list_user_id.description: Foreign key to the owning user account. Links session to the specific end-user in the todo_list_users table. Not exposed or mutable via API; used internally for strict data isolation and access control.

ip.description: IP address used during the establishment of this session, as recorded at authentication. Enables audit trails and security tracing for the user's logins.

href.description: Full connection URL (the page or route the user was accessing when the session was started). Provides context for understanding the origin of the session. Required for security and forensic analysis.

referrer.description: Referrer URL captured at session start, showing the source page or external site involved in the login event. Supports audit and behavioral analysis.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was first created and authenticated. Used for chronological sorting, session lifespan analysis, and security monitoring.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was terminated. Null indicates an active session. Allows accurate history tracking and supports detection of concurrent or stale sessions.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description: Flexible filtering, searching, and pagination parameters for querying a user's own session records in the Todo List application.

created_from.description: Only include sessions created after or on this timestamp (ISO 8601 date-time). Leave null to omit the earliest date filter.

created_to.description: Only include sessions created before or on this timestamp (ISO 8601 date-time). Leave null to omit the latest date filter.

expired_from.description: Only include sessions expired after or on this timestamp (ISO 8601 date-time). Leave null to omit the earliest expiry filter.

expired_to.description: Only include sessions expired before or on this timestamp (ISO 8601 date-time). Leave null to omit the latest expiry filter.

ip.description: Filter to include only sessions established from this IP address. Leave empty to include all IPs.

href.description: Filter to include only sessions started from this specific connection URL. Leave empty to include all URLs.

referrer.description: Filter to include only sessions with this exact referrer URL at login. Leave empty to include all referrers.

page.description: Page number for pagination of session results. 1-based index (first page is 1).

limit.description: Maximum number of session records to return per page. Used for paginated queries; capped at 100 to prevent performance issues.

search.description: Textual search string that matches todo title or description. Supports partial matches and case-insensitive queries. Optional; omitting means no text search.

completed.description: If present, filters todos by their completion status. true to show only completed, false to show only uncompleted, omit for both.

dueDateFrom.description: Lower bound (inclusive, ISO 8601 UTC) for filtering todos by their due date. Optional; null means no lower bound is applied.

dueDateTo.description: Upper bound (inclusive, ISO 8601 UTC) for due date filtering. Optional; null means no upper bound is applied.

createdFrom.description: Lower bound (inclusive, ISO 8601 UTC) for filtering todos by creation date. Optional.

createdTo.description: Upper bound (inclusive, ISO 8601 UTC) for creation date filtering. Optional.

oneOf.description: Sort key for result ordering. Supported: created_at, due_date, title. Optional; defaults to created_at.
Sort key for result ordering. Supported: created_at, due_date, title. Optional; defaults to created_at.
Sort key for result ordering. Supported: created_at, due_date, title. Optional; defaults to created_at.

sortBy.description: Sort key for result ordering. Supported: created_at, due_date, title. Optional; defaults to created_at.

oneOf.description: Sort direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending order. Defaults to descending.
Sort direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending order. Defaults to descending.

sortOrder.description: Sort direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending order. Defaults to descending.

page.description: Page number to retrieve, starting from 1. Required for pagination.

pageSize.description: Page size for pagination; max 100 for server-side performance. Required.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching, filtering, sorting, and paginating the user's todo tasks in the Todo List Application.

Supports text search, completion status, due/creation date range filters, sort options, and pagination. Used in PATCH /todoList/user/todos for listing todos.

id.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each todo. Assigned on creation and immutable.

title.description: Required short textual title for the todo. Must be present and between 1 and 100 characters, per application validation. Cannot be empty.

oneOf.description: Optional longer plaintext description of this todo. Up to 600 characters if present.
Description may be omitted or explicitly set to null.

description.description: Optional longer plaintext description of this todo. Up to 600 characters if present. Null or omitted if not supplied.

completed.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the todo is completed. Defaults to false at creation; toggled via update API.

oneOf.description: Optional ISO8601 date by which the todo is expected to be completed, in UTC. Null if not set.
due_date is null if not provided.

due_date.description: Optional due date for the todo, in ISO 8601 UTC format. Null if not set.

created_at.description: Timestamp in UTC when the todo was created. Used for sorting, filtering, and audit history.

updated_at.description: Timestamp in UTC of most recent modification. Automatically updated on changes.

todo_list_user_id.description: Owner user for this todo task. Foreign key to todo_list_users.id. Strictly enforced; immutable after creation.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Business tasks (todos) that form the core entity of the Todo List Application.

Each represents a single actionable task, always owned by a user with enforced foreign key and business rules. Includes required title, optional description, completion status, and optional due date. Includes audit timestamps for creation/update. Ownership is immutable; todos cannot be delegated or shared. Used in GET/PUT /todoList/user/todos/{todoId} and POST (response).

title.description: The required title for the todo task. Must be a non-empty plain text string (1–100 characters). Leading and trailing whitespace is disallowed; blank titles are invalid. Required by the business rules for every todo creation request.

oneOf.description: Optional longer textual description giving additional context for the todo. If supplied, must not exceed 600 characters. Leading/trailing whitespace is permitted, and field may be omitted or set to null if not needed.
Field set to null if not needed.

description.description: Optional longer textual description giving additional context for the todo. If supplied, must not exceed 600 characters. Leading/trailing whitespace is permitted, and field may be omitted or set to null if not needed.

oneOf.description: Optional due date by which the todo should be completed. Must be an ISO 8601 formatted string and be today or a future date if supplied. If omitted or null, the todo has no strict due date.
Field set to null if no due date is being provided.

due_date.description: Optional due date by which the todo should be completed. Must be an ISO 8601 formatted string and be today or a future date if supplied. If omitted or null, the todo has no strict due date.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description: Data required for creating a new todo task. The caller must supply a valid title (1–100 characters); an optional description (up to 600 characters) and due date (ISO 8601 today or future) may be provided. Completion status is always initialized as false at create-time. The todo is automatically assigned to the authenticated user, with ownership not settable by client. Strict uniqueness is enforced on (title + due_date) per user to prevent duplicate tasks. Ownership, timing, and forbidden fields are handled by the backend, not included here.

title.description: If specified, the new title for the todo item. Must follow the same rules as creation (1–100 characters, cannot be blank). Field is optional; omit or null if not changing the title.

oneOf.description: Optional updated description. If specified, must not exceed 600 characters. Field may be omitted or set to null if not being changed.
Field set to null to explicitly remove any existing description.

description.description: Optional updated description. If specified, must not exceed 600 characters. Field may be omitted or set to null if not being changed.

completed.description: If specified, sets the completion status of the todo item. Must be true or false. Field is optional; if omitted, status remains unchanged.

oneOf.description: Optional updated due date in ISO 8601 format. If specified, must be today or a future date. If null, explicitly removes the due date from the todo.
Field set to null to explicitly remove due date.

due_date.description: Optional updated due date in ISO 8601 format. If specified, must be today or a future date. If null, explicitly removes the due date from the todo.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description: Fields that may be updated on an existing todo task. All fields are optional and can be provided in any combination. Title (if supplied) must be 1–100 characters and non-blank. Description (if supplied) must not exceed 600 characters. Completed status (if supplied) must be boolean. Due date (if supplied) must be an ISO 8601 date string representing today or a future date, or null to delete existing due date. No field may be set to an invalid value. Any omitted property will remain unchanged.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a Todo List task for efficient list API responses.

Captures the essential details needed to display a todo record in lists, dashboards, and lightweight UI contexts. Excludes larger descriptive content and strong composition arrays for optimal performance.

Represents a business user's owned task, with required and optional fields reflecting current status and scheduling. Each summary record is linked to its owner and includes the owner's unique ID for context; actual ownership detail comes from the user context or additional queries.

Includes immutable, non-sensitive fields only: contains no private or write-only data. Incorporates audit fields for creation and modification time to support history, filtering, and UI updates. Designed for robust sorting and UI timeline functionality.

id.description: Unique identifier of the todo task. Primary key from the database; unguessable and immutable.

todo_list_user_id.description: Owner user for this todo task. Foreign key referencing the user who owns this record. Each todo is strictly privately owned and only accessible by this user.

title.description: Short, required title summarizing the todo task. Required, always present. Maximum 100 characters.

completed.description: Boolean indicating whether the todo task is complete. True if completed, false otherwise. Default is false.

due_date.description: Optional due date/time by which the todo is expected to be completed, in ISO 8601 format. Null if not set. Must be a present or future date if present.

created_at.description: Timestamp in UTC when the todo was created. Used for sorting, filtering, and audit trail purposes. Set automatically by the system at creation.

updated_at.description: Timestamp in UTC when the todo was last updated. Tracks most recent modification for UI refresh and sorting. Updated automatically by the application on change.
